$comment: OpenCodeForge hand-curated additions overlaid onto the upstream opencode-tui.json schema at load time via SchemaRegistry.ApplyOverlay (RFC 7396 JSON Merge Patch semantics). Same mechanism, and same rules, as claude-code-settings.overlay.json — read that file's SAFETY note first. Today this carries exactly one addition: `theme`, whose upstream declaration is the bare `{"type":"string"}` with NO description and NO examples, so the generic dispatch renders it as an unlabelled text box and the user has no way to learn what a valid theme name is. `theme.examples` promotes it to the free-form AutoCompleteBox (SchemaTreeBuilder treats a string with examples and no enum as an enum that allows typing), and `theme.description` states where themes come from. === WHY examples IS ONLY ["opencode"] === Because that is the only built-in TUI theme name that could be VERIFIED. Measured against the installed opencode v1.17.9 binary: the TUI theme store is initialised `active:"opencode"` and its source is the disk-scan discover function, so every other theme comes from a themes/*.json file or a plugin rather than from a built-in table. A 37-name list DOES exist in that binary (`zU`, ids to display names, e.g. dracula/nord/tokyonight) but it sits with `setColorScheme`, `previewThemeId` and the `oc-2` default — that is the WEB UI's theme provider, not the TUI's. Suggesting those names here would assert something measurement had already disproven. The remaining suggestions are added at runtime by OpenCodeEditorFactory from the user's own themes directory, which is verifiable, so the picker is honest at both ends. === SAFETY === RFC 7396 makes overlay keys unconditionally win and a null deletes the matched key. This overlay must stay ADDITIVE — description/examples/default only. Do NOT add `pattern`, `enum`, `required`, `const`, `minLength` or `maxLength` here: the TUI schema's own constraints must survive the merge byte-for-byte, and the keybinds subtree in particular is a 924-union tree whose `enum: [false]` arms are what stop this app offering values OpenCode rejects. `default` is deliberately ABSENT even though `opencode` is the initial active theme: a schema `default` drives a '(inherits: <x>)' watermark, which is a claim about what OpenCode does when the key is absent, and the binary's two candidate defaults disagree across surfaces (`opencode` in the TUI store, `oc-2` in the web provider). Not verified, so not asserted.

theme.description: Colour theme for the terminal UI. `opencode` is the built-in default. Additional themes are JSON files picked up from a `themes/` directory beside the OpenCode config, or from a `.opencode/themes/` directory in the working directory or any parent of it; a plugin can also supply them. The theme name is the file name without its `.json` extension. Any name is accepted here — the suggestions are the built-in theme plus whatever this machine's OpenCode config directory contains, not a limit.
